name: IL-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Republican candidate's minimal fundraising ($58k, $42 cash on hand)
Open seat after Danny Davis's retirement, but Democratic nominee well-funded
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: This Chicago-based seat carries a +34 Democratic partisan lean, and the Republican nominee has raised only about $58,000 with essentially no cash on hand, while Democrat La Shawn Ford has out-raised him more than tenfold and benefits from outside spending on his side. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays firmly in Safe D territory with a margin near the district's fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise surge in Republican fundraising or outside spending, or an unexpected scandal involving the Democratic nominee, would be the main things to watch.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Danny Davis (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Danny Davis's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat open, but the district's +34 Democratic partisan lean makes a Republican takeover extremely unlikely. Democrat La Shawn Ford has raised over $720,000 and has outside spending supporting him, while Republican Chad Koppie has raised under $60,000 and reported just $42 in cash on hand.

Prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's win probability near 97%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals and the stark resource gap, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
